info.title: SEOCart REST API
info.description: The routes of the `seocart/v1` namespace, and of the Store API, `seocart/store/v1`, whose paths name their own server. Each operation is generated from the same declaration as its ability and its WP-CLI command, which docs/reference/ describes. A request authenticates as a WordPress user, with a REST nonce or an application password, and each operation names the capability it requires. A Store API operation requires none: anyone may send a read, and a write must satisfy the Store API's request policy.

post.summary: Applies a promotion code to the cart, when its promotion applies to the cart now, and answers the cart with the discount in its totals. A cart holds at most 5 codes. A code that cannot be applied gets promotion.code_invalid, the same answer whatever the reason; after 10 codes tried on one cart in an hour, or 40 by one client, every code is refused with store_api.rate_limited until the hour ends.

post.summary: Switches the request's cart to another currency the store sells in, at the cart version the client read: the switch moves the version on, drops the checkout's shipping and tax quotes, keeps the shipping method chosen, and answers the cart priced in the new currency; a switch to the currency the cart is in already is accepted like any other. A cart placing an order refuses it with cart.not_open, a cart switches at most 10 times in an hour, and a currency the store does not sell in gets checkout.currency_not_enabled, whatever the reason.

post.summary: Places an order from the request's cart, at the cart version and for the grand total the client read, and has its payment authorized; the Idempotency-Key header is required. A retry with the same key never places a second order: it is answered 200 with the placement as it stands now, the same order and order key, its outcome and statuses as the settlement left them, and a declined placement is answered so too, with the outcome declined, since refusals are not kept.
post.description: Public: requires no capability. The Store API's request policy requires the header `X-SEOCart-Store: 1`, the `X-WP-Nonce` header when a login cookie is sent, the cart's token, and at most 5 requests per client in 3600 seconds.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: The attempt's idempotency key, sent in the Idempotency-Key header and nowhere else: a new key, such as a UUID, for each attempt, and the same key when it is retried.

cart_version.description: The version of the cart the write is based on: the version of the last answer.

grand_total_minor.description: The grand total the shopper agreed to, in minor units of the cart's currency, as the cart's last answer gave it; a cart whose total is now another is refused with checkout.totals_changed.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the cart's currency, as the cart's last answer gave it.

payment_token.description: The gateway's token for the shopper's payment method, never a card number.

payment_data.description: What the client sends the payment gateway, such as the token of the shopper's payment method.

200.description: The operation succeeded. The body is the Placement resource.

The request does not match the input schema: `rest_invalid_param` or `rest_missing_callback_param`.

`checkout.session_incomplete`: The checkout is missing details an order needs: both addresses, an email address on the billing address, and a payment method. The error lists the ones missing.

post.summary: Changes the units on hand of one variant by a signed amount, records the change in the stock ledger with its reason, and returns the stock level after it.

parameters.name: variant_id
parameters.description: The id of the variant whose stock is adjusted.

delta.description: The change of the units on hand: positive for units that arrived, negative for units that left; never 0.

reason.description: Why the units on hand changed.

expected_on_hand.description: The units on hand the client last read. When given, the change applies only while the variant still has exactly that many, so a repeated request cannot apply it twice.

200.description: The operation succeeded. The body is the StockLevel resource.

400.description:
The request does not match the input schema: `rest_invalid_param` or `rest_missing_callback_param`.

`stock.zero_delta`: An adjustment of zero units changes nothing. To confirm a count, adjust by the difference you found.

`stock.on_hand_conflict`: Variant {variant_id}: you expected {expected} on hand, but there are {on_hand}, so the adjustment was not applied. Read the stock again, then repeat the adjustment if it is still needed.

`stock.adjustment_below_zero`: Variant {variant_id} has {on_hand} on hand, so a change of {delta} would take it below zero.

version.description: The cart's version: 0 when there is no cart, then one more after every accepted write. Send it with the next write, and discard an answer whose version is lower than one already seen.

quantity.description: How many units of the variant: a line holds at most 99999, and units added beyond fill it to that.

code.description: The promotion code, as the store spells it.

Error.description: An error. WordPress writes it as its code, its message and its data; the data members are the same for every error of these routes, including WordPress's own refusal of a request that does not match the input schema or of a user who lacks the capability, but not its refusal of a JSONP callback, which it sends before any route is matched.

code.description: The error code: one of those in docs/reference/errors.md, or a code of the WordPress REST API such as `rest_invalid_param` or `rest_forbidden`.

message.description: What went wrong, for people, in the language of the site. An internal error has a generic message.

status.description: The HTTP status of the error.

details.description: The values the message was built from, keyed by name. For an error WordPress raised, such as its refusal of a request that does not match the input schema, every other member of its data under the name WordPress gave it, such as `params`; WordPress's own per-parameter `details` is flattened into `param_codes`, one code for each parameter WordPress gave a code, omitted when there is none, so nothing named `details` ever nests inside `details`. Always an object, and empty for an internal error.

correlation_id.description: The identifier of the request the error happened in, which the site's log records with the error; null when the request has none.

order_uuid.description: The order's public identifier, by which its status is read.

order_number.description: The number shown to people on the order and in its emails.

order_key.description: The order's access key, which reads its status without a login, as the status read's order_key. It is shown in this answer, and again to a retry of the same request only: to the holder of the cart token and of the idempotency key it was placed with, since the store keeps the key only as a hash and sealed with those two, which it never keeps. Send a random idempotency key, such as a UUID. A retry whose kept key cannot be opened is answered without it; the client must keep it.

cart_version.description: The cart's version once the order was placed.

outcome.description: What the placement came to: approved, requires_action when the shopper must act, processing while the gateway decides, or, given to a retry with the same key, any outcome the placement came to since, declined included; pending only while the payment is not yet known.

status.description: The order's status once the placement settled.

payment_status.description: How far the order is paid once the placement settled.

base_currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency the store keeps its accounts in, in upper case.

cross_zone_policy.description: What stays fixed when a price entered including tax is sold where the tax rate differs from the store's own: fixed_net keeps the price before tax, fixed_gross keeps the price paid.

tax_rounding_mode.description: Where tax is rounded: per_line rounds each line's tax, per_subtotal rounds the tax of the lines of one tax class once and shares it out to them.

variant_id.description: The id of the variant whose stock is adjusted.

on_hand.description: The units physically in stock after the change.

allocated.description: The units promised to accepted orders.

held.description: The units held by checkouts, expired holds included until they are reclaimed.

available.description: The units that may still be promised: on hand, less allocated, less held. Negative when fewer units were counted than are promised or held.

ledger_entry_id.description: The id of the stock ledger entry that records the change.

order_number.description: The number shown to people on the order and in its emails; a request never names an order by it.

status.description: Where the order is in its life, from pending payment to completed.

payment_status.description: How far the order has been paid, or refunded.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the currency every amount is in.

subtotal_minor.description: The lines before discounts, in minor units.

grand_total_minor.description: The order's total, in minor units.

paid_minor.description: What has been captured so far, in minor units.

refunded_minor.description: What has been refunded so far, in minor units.

due_minor.description: What is still to be paid, in minor units.

title.description: The product's name as it was sold.

variant_label.description: The variant as it was sold, such as a size; empty for a product without variants.

sku.description: The SKU as it was sold.

line_total_minor.description: The line's total as the order shows it, in minor units.

lines.description: The order's lines, in their order.

nonce.description: A fresh wp_rest nonce for the user the request was authenticated as. Send it as the X-WP-Nonce header of the next request.

user_id.description: The WordPress user the request was authenticated as; 0 for a guest, and for a request that carried a login cookie without a nonce.
